title: SDK Garden: micro-playlist hypotheses and quick labs
content:
Purpose
---
Notes for a lightweight, modular "SDK Garden" concept: a set of short, opinionated micro-playlists (guided sequences of 2–6 tiny steps) that get an engineer from zero to a small integrated feature in 10–40 minutes. Goal: reduce time-to-first-success, increase observable success metrics, and create repeatable classroom-style labs for self-serve and SE-led onboarding.

Why 'garden'?
- Small plots (micro-guides) that are independent, composable, and easy to iterate on.
- Low friction: each plot should have one measurable outcome.
- Encourage experimentation and remixing (seed templates + soil = user app).

Target personas
- Backend engineer adding a Redwood text-generation route to an existing API (10–25 min).
- Frontend engineer wiring a streaming chat component to Redwood (20–45 min).
- Platform engineer testing Dedicated capacity with a simple throughput test (30–60 min).
- SE/trial user who wants a quick demo to show a product manager (10–20 min).

High-level structure for each micro-playlist
1) One-line outcome (what success looks like).
2) Prereqs (expected familiarity, required tokens/keys, minimal infra).
3) Steps (sequential, minimal copy-paste snippets).
4) Validation checks (curl commands, smoke checks, screenshot hints).
5) Telemetry to observe (events + where to look in Console).
6) Failure modes & recovery tips (common errors and fixes).
7) Next steps (how to expand the mini-feature).

Proposed micro-playlists (hypotheses)
- quick-text-endpoint: create a single POST /generate that returns text from Redwood (outcome: working endpoint w/ test harness). 10–15m.
- streaming-chat-widget: wire a small React component to Redwood streaming API. Outcome: streaming tokens appear in UI. 20–30m.
- embed-search-prototype: index 200 docs into embeddings and run a nearest-neighbor search endpoint. Outcome: top-K hits returned. 25–40m.
- cheap-batching-demo: modify a small client to use batching preset and measure token cost drop. Outcome: >20% cost reduction on synthetic load. 30–45m.
- canary-fallback-flow: configure route to fallback from large model -> quantized variant under latency pressure. Outcome: fallback logged and visible in Console. 20–30m.
- local-vs-hosted-sanity: replicate a hosted API call with local Redwood Private runtime (VPC stub). Outcome: identical response sanity check. 30–60m.

Example micro-playlist: quick-text-endpoint (sketch)
- outcome: POST /generate replies with text from redwood-hosted model within 300ms p50 on local test.
- prereqs: Redwood API key, Node 18+, minimal Express app.
- steps:
  1) npm init && npm i express axios
  2) create server.js with simple POST handler that proxies to Redwood API (snippet below).
  3) curl local endpoint using sample prompt file and assert response contains 'assistant'.
- validation:
  - curl -sS localhost:3000/generate -d '@sample-prompt.json' | jq .choices[0].text
  - check Console -> per-route latency graph (route: quick-text-endpoint)
- telemetry to add:
  - event: quick_text_request.started
  - metric: quick_text_request.latency_ms (p50/p95)
  - tag: model_variant
- failure modes:
  - 401 from Redwood: verify key env var and minimal token scope
  - 429 rate limit: show how to enable retries with exponential backoff

Lab scripts and artifacts
- seed repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdkgarden-starters (placeholder PR linked above).
- sample prompts: short, safe, test-friendly prompts for each playlist. Keep them deterministic for smoke tests.
- local test harness: light Python harness + curl scripts for CI smoke checks.

Telemetry and gating (how we’ll know these help)
- Success metrics to track per-playlist:
  - completion rate (user reaches final validation step in guide) — instrument via 'doc:play_complete' event in quickstart pages.
  - time-to-first-success (from onboarding start to validation pass) — measured by SE-run feedback and UX telemetry.
  - reduction in support threads tagged "onboarding: sdk" after playlists shipped.
  - number of forks/stars on sdkgarden-starters repo.
- Gating for GA: completion_rate >= 45% on self-serve cohort and < 10 support tickets per 100 new signups for the covered flows.

Tone + pedagogy notes
- Keep text conversational and prescriptive (do this, not just explain theory).
- Prefer copy-paste code snippets with minimal editing.
- Add short "why this matters" callouts to connect to cost/latency observability.
- Provide condensed "cheat sheet" at top plus optional deep-dive links.

Open questions / experiments to run
- Which 3 playlists to ship first to maximize demoability for Enterprise trials? Hypothesis: streaming-chat-widget + embed-search-prototype + quick-text-endpoint. Need A/B test.
- Should we wire the validation step to create an ephemeral Dedicated job to show autoscaling? Complexity vs benefit tradeoff.
- Can we automate snippet generation for multiple languages using the same canonical flow? (Node, Python, Go)
- Minimal telemetry SDK contract: what events are strictly required vs nice-to-have? (See TODO below)

Appendix: tiny Node proxy snippet (for quick-text-endpoint)
const express = require('express');
const axios = require('axios');
const app = express();
app.use(express.json());
app.post('/generate', async (req, res) => {
  try {
    const r = await axios.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', { prompt: req.body.prompt }, { headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}` } });
    res.json({ ok: true, text: r.data.choices?.[0]?.text || '' });
  } catch (e) {
    console.error(e?.response?.data || e.message);
    res.status(500).json({ ok: false, error: 'proxy-error' });
  }
});
app.listen(3000, () => console.log('listening'));

Notes-to-self
- Keep playlists intentionally opinionated — reduce choices.
- Iterate quickly: convert one playlist into a workshop for SEs, then fold feedback into next revision.
- Avoid long conceptual docs here; instead link to product docs for deep dives.

End of sketch.
